newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian LUKoil in group to upgrade Norsi refinery.
newsitem.headline: Russian LUKoil in group to upgrade Norsi refinery.

text.p: The Russian government has approved a proposal by Russia's largest oil producer, LUKoil, and others to form a financial-industrial group to modernise the Norsi oil refinery, a government decree said on Wednesday.

The document, signed by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and published in the Rossiiskaya Gazeta government newspaper, said LUKoil, independent oil company Norsi-Oil, Alfa-Bank and financial concern Rusintern would form the group, to be called the Volzhskaya (Volga) Company.
Norsi, an independent oil company, comprises four marketing facilities in Nizhny Novgorod and the city's refinery. It has no production or exploration units.
The refinery currently processes about 312,000 barrels per day. It refined 12.5 million tonnes (250,000 bpd) in 1995.

It said in March that it was seeking to build a new, high-yield complex to process about four million tonnes of oil a year (80,000 barrels per day) and to upgrade its ethylene and polyethylene petrochemical units.
The government is due to sell a 34 percent stake in Norsi-Oil this year.
